climate-security-2021-12-13.visible-2: India sought to preserve the universal, consensus-based UNFCCC process for climate decisions, arguing that most developing nations lack a voice in the Security Council. Instead, it supported a narrower alternative draft limited specifically to climate pressures in the Sahel region.
climate-security-2021-12-13.visible-3: Russia opposed an automatic climate-security link, preferring substantive work at the UNFCCC and a draft focused on the Sahel. India opposed moving climate decisions to the Security Council, favoring a narrower alternative limited to the Sahel region. Both delegations supported a Sahel-specific alternative while rejecting a universal Security Council approach.
climate-security-2021-12-13.visible-4: China abstained to support country-specific Council consideration of climate risks in peace and security rather than treating climate change as a universal security challenge. It emphasized common but differentiated responsibilities, urging developed nations to fulfill financing, technology transfer, and capacity-building commitments.
climate-security-2021-12-13.visible-5: Russia opposed the draft's automatic climate-security link, preferring Sahel-specific analysis and work through the UNFCCC. China abstained, favoring country-specific risk assessment and emphasizing common but differentiated responsibilities for climate action.
climate-security-2021-12-13.visible-6: India sought to preserve the universal, consensus-based UNFCCC process and supported a narrower alternative limited to the Sahel region. China preserved its principle of country-specific Council consideration and its commitment to common but differentiated responsibilities for climate action.
